## 1. Document.Bot​

Document.Bot is built for source-backed work across real folders. You connect a local folder of PDFs, Word documents, spreadsheets, Markdown, and notes. Document.Bot indexes the workspace locally, lets you search across exact keywords and approximate descriptions, and helps you tag source material into the assistant.

That matters because many questions are cross-format:

A PDF assistant is useful for PDF tasks. A folder workspace is useful when the answer is distributed.

## 2. ChatGPT​

ChatGPT is a good Acrobat AI Assistant alternative when the task is small and upload-friendly. OpenAI's file upload docs describe workflows such as summarizing documents, comparing files, extracting information, and analyzing spreadsheets: OpenAI file uploads FAQ. [...] ## The Short Answer​

Use Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant when your primary job is PDF reading, summarization, editing, organizing, and PDF-centric collaboration. Use Document.Bot when the work crosses file types and you need a local-first AI workspace for folders, citations, source selection, and reviewable drafts.

Adobe describes Acrobat AI Assistant as a way to ask questions, generate summaries, get insights, and receive cited responses in document workflows. Adobe also describes PDF Spaces for combining files and links into an AI-powered workspace: Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant.

That is useful. The practical question is whether your document problem is PDF-first or folder-first.

No. Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant is designed specifically for document analysis and interaction. For general brainstorming, content creation, research, and broad conversational assistance, Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT Edu may be a better option. Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant is most effective when working with existing documents.

## Should I verify AI-generated responses?

Yes. Like all generative AI tools, Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant may produce inaccurate or incomplete responses. Users are responsible for reviewing and validating AI-generated content before using it for academic, administrative, research, or business purposes.

## Are documents uploaded to Adobe and then used with the AI assistant, retained or used as training material? [...] ## Frequently Asked Questions

## Does Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant have access to my files?

No. Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant only has access to documents that you open or upload within Adobe Acrobat.

## Can Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant summarize documents?

Yes. Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant can generate summaries, identify key takeaways, extract action items, and answer questions about document content. Responses include references back to the source document to help users verify information.
